description: Move the alt-text and crop modals out of example/ and into the image-input component, so consumers get both dialogs for free instead of rebuilding the wiring. Dialogs are native <dialog> elements that fade and scale in on open. image-input:edit and image-input:alt keep firing and stay cancelable, so the existing bring-your-own-dialog path still works. Detailed spec and rationale live in specs/tasks/component-dialogs.md; read it before starting. The components stay on @substrate-system/web-component -- microtags is a dependency in package.json but is NOT used by this work.

userStories.title: The component renders its own alt and crop dialogs
userStories.description: As a consuming developer, I want image-input to render the two dialogs itself, so I do not have to write dialog markup to use the component.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/dialogs.ts exports the markup builders for the alt dialog and the crop dialog, plus small open/close helpers; src/index.ts keeps the event wiring
render() emits both <dialog> elements as siblings of .box, inside image-input, closed by default
The alt dialog contains a heading, a <label> that wraps its own <textarea rows="4">, and a menu with .alt-cancel and .alt-save buttons
The crop dialog contains a heading, an empty .crop-slot div, and a menu with .crop-cancel and .crop-save buttons
ImageInput gains a static TEXT object with altHeading, altLabel, cropHeading, save and cancel keys, read at render time
There are no id or for attributes and no aria-labelledby anywhere in the dialog markup; each dialog carries aria-label instead
The textarea has no name attribute and every dialog button is type="button", so an image-input inside a <form> submits exactly what it did before
A test asserts two image-input elements on one page each render their own two dialogs and produce no duplicate ids
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: No ids is a hard requirement, not a style preference: ten image-input elements on a page would otherwise emit ten duplicate ids. Implicit labelling is valid here because a textarea is the label's own control -- see the existing note in src/AGENTS.md about labelable descendants. src/index.ts is 282 lines before this work; the dialogs.ts split exists to keep it from passing 400. esbuild src/*.ts is not bundled and the exports map has a ./* catch-all, so a new source file needs no build change.

userStories.title: The ALT badge opens the built-in alt dialog
userStories.description: As a user, I want clicking the ALT badge to open a dialog with the current alt text, so I can edit it without the page author wiring anything up.
acceptanceCriteria: handleAlt still emits image-input:alt with its current detail payload before opening anything
When the event is not canceled, the alt dialog's textarea is seeded from that element's current alt value and the dialog is opened with showModal()
Both open paths check dialog.open first, because showModal() throws InvalidStateError on an already-open dialog
The textarea is the first focusable element in the dialog, so showModal()'s native autofocus lands on it with no explicit focus() call
The new listeners are attached in setupEventListeners and removed in disconnectedCallback, alongside the existing .remove, .edit and .alt-badge listeners
A test asserts that clicking .alt-badge with a file loaded sets dialog.open to true and that the textarea value equals the element's alt
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The two Cancel buttons must keep distinct class names (.alt-cancel, .crop-cancel), and likewise .alt-save and .crop-save. this.qs() is querySelector() and returns only the first match, so a shared .dialog-cancel class would wire one dialog's Cancel and leave the other silently dead.

userStories.title: Saving alt text updates the element
userStories.description: As a user, I want Save to apply my alt text and Cancel to discard it, so the dialog behaves the way dialogs normally do.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking .alt-save assigns the textarea value to this.alt and closes the dialog
Assigning this.alt goes through the existing handleChange_alt, so image-input:alt-change fires and the img alt attribute and badge has-alt state update with no new code
Clicking .alt-cancel closes the dialog and leaves alt unchanged, and emits nothing
Pressing Esc closes the dialog and leaves alt unchanged, via native <dialog> behavior with no key handler
No new event types are added
Tests assert the save path sets alt and emits image-input:alt-change, and that the cancel path closes the dialog with alt unchanged
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Tests must assert behavior, not rendered text: check dialog.open and the alt property, never the button or heading strings.

userStories.title: The edit button opens a crop dialog with a lazily created image-crop
userStories.description: As a user, I want clicking edit to open a crop dialog, and as a developer I do not want idle crop machinery on pages where nobody crops.
acceptanceCriteria: src/index.ts gains import './crop.js', so importing image-input defines both image-input and image-crop
handleEdit still emits image-input:edit with its current detail payload before opening anything
No <image-crop> element exists anywhere in the DOM until the crop dialog is opened for the first time
On first open, an <image-crop> is created and appended to .crop-slot, then setFile() is called with the current file and the dialog is opened with showModal()
On subsequent opens the existing <image-crop> is reused and only setFile() and showModal() are called
A test asserts no image-crop exists before the first edit click and exactly one exists after it
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: ImageCrop.connectedCallback attaches four window listeners (resize, pointermove, pointerup, pointercancel). Rendering an image-crop eagerly inside every image-input would mean forty idle window listeners on a page with ten inputs. The lazily created element is left in place after close so reopening is cheap, and it unregisters naturally when the host image-input disconnects and takes the subtree with it.

userStories.title: Saving the crop replaces the image
userStories.description: As a user, I want Save in the crop dialog to apply my crop to the preview, so the crop flow completes without the page author writing any glue.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking .crop-save calls getBlob() on the image-crop, passes the resulting Blob to this.setImage(blob), then closes the dialog
setImage() already emits image-input:change and already syncs input.files, so no new event and no new file plumbing is added
Clicking .crop-cancel closes the dialog and leaves the current image and file unchanged
Pressing Esc closes the dialog and leaves the current image and file unchanged
A test asserts that the crop save path emits image-input:change and closes the dialog
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: getBlob() returns a Promise, so the save handler is async and the dialog closes only after the blob resolves. Tests must await it.

userStories.title: Consumers can opt out of the built-in dialogs
userStories.description: As a consuming developer with my own crop or alt UI, I want to suppress the built-in dialogs, so upgrading does not force the component's UI on me.
acceptanceCriteria: Calling preventDefault() on image-input:edit stops the crop dialog opening and creates no image-crop element
Calling preventDefault() on image-input:alt stops the alt dialog opening
Both handlers read emit()'s boolean return and bail early when it is false, rather than inspecting the event object
setImage() and the alt property remain public and unchanged, so the opt-out path is still complete
Tests assert that a canceling listener on each event leaves the corresponding dialog closed
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: WebComponent.emit() already defaults to { bubbles: true, cancelable: true } and returns false when a listener calls preventDefault(), so this is a two-line change per handler and needs no change to the emit call sites.

userStories.title: Dialogs fade and scale in when they open
userStories.description: As a user, I want the dialogs to fade in rather than snap into place, so opening one does not feel jarring.
acceptanceCriteria: src/index.css styles the dialogs nested under the existing image-input block, so the rules cannot match a consumer's own dialogs

The dialog transitions opacity 0 to 1 and transform scale(var(--image-input-dialog-scale-from)) to scale(1), with transition-property listing opacity, transform, display and overlay, and transition-behavior: allow-discrete written after any shorthand
The entry animation uses @starting-style nested inside the &[open] rule
The backdrop transitions from transparent to --image-input-dialog-backdrop-color with its own @starting-style inside &[open]::backdrop

src/_vars.css gains --image-input-dialog-bg, --image-input-dialog-radius defaulting to var(--image-input-radius), --image-input-dialog-padding, --image-input-dialog-max-width, --image-input-dialog-backdrop-color, --image-input-dialog-duration set to 250ms, and --image-input-dialog-scale-from set to 0.95
Every color and size in the new CSS comes from a variable, and existing variables are reused rather than duplicated
A prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block drops the transform and cuts the duration to 0.01ms, and does NOT set transition: none
stylelint passes on src/*.css
No CSS unrelated to the dialogs is changed
userStories.notes: Top-layer promotion changes painting and stacking, not the DOM tree, so image-input dialog and image-input dialog::backdrop keep matching while the dialog is open. Reduced motion must not use transition: none, because allow-discrete still has to fire for the dialog to become visible at all. 250ms and 0.95 match @substrate-system/dialog's SHOW-OVERLAY and SHOW-DIALOG keyframes. @starting-style and transition-behavior are Baseline since 2024-08-06; overlay is Chromium-only, so Firefox and Safari get the entry fade and an instant exit, which is acceptable because only an entry animation is specified.

userStories.title: Documentation and example reflect the built-in dialogs
userStories.description: As a consuming developer, I want the README and demo to show that the dialogs come with the component, so I can tell what I get without reading the source.
acceptanceCriteria: README gains a section describing the two built-in dialogs and the static TEXT object for changing their copy
README's image-input:edit and image-input:alt entries document that both are cancelable and that preventDefault() suppresses the built-in dialog
README's existing 'open a crop dialog, then setImage(croppedBlob)' snippet is reframed as the documented opt-out rather than the default path
README's CSS variable list gains the seven new --image-input-dialog-* variables
example/index.ts drops its dialog markup and all its dialog wiring, keeping the image-input element and the alt-change display
example/index.css drops the rules for the removed #crop-dialog and #alt-dialog
src/AGENTS.md gains notes on why the dialogs use no ids, why image-crop is created lazily, the distinct-class-per-button reason, and the overlay support caveat
npm test passes end to end
userStories.notes: Do not write tests for documentation. The example rewrite onto preact, @preact/signals and htm is a separate piece of work with its own spec, and starts from the smaller example/index.ts this story leaves behind.
